result.topic_en: Contiguous relations of the hypergeometric series F(α,β,γ) and its derivative F′, expressing F and F′ with parameters shifted by ±1 rationally in terms of F(α,β,γ) and F′(α,β,γ).
result.transcription:
[4] $F'(\alpha+1,\beta,\gamma) = \frac{\beta}{1-x}F(\alpha,\beta,\gamma) + \frac{(\alpha-\gamma+1+\beta x)}{\alpha(1-x)}F'(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$
und eben so ist offenbar
[5] $F'(\alpha,\beta+1,\gamma) = \frac{\alpha}{1-x}F(\alpha,\beta,\gamma) + \frac{\beta-\gamma+1+\alpha x}{\beta(1-x)}F'(\alpha,\beta,x)$
Aus der Verbindung von 2 und 4 schliessen wir ferner
[6] $F(\alpha-1,\beta,\gamma) = \frac{\alpha-\gamma+\beta x}{\alpha-\gamma}F(\alpha,\beta,\gamma) - \frac{[?](x-xx)}{\alpha-\gamma}F'(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$
und eben so
[7] $F(\alpha,\beta-1,\gamma) = \frac{\beta-\gamma+\alpha x}{\beta-\gamma}F(\alpha,\beta,\gamma) - \frac{(\beta-1)[?](x-xx)}{\beta-\gamma}F'(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$
[8] $F'(\alpha-1,\beta,\gamma) = -\frac{(\alpha-1)\beta}{\alpha-\gamma}F(\alpha,\beta,\gamma) + \frac{(\alpha-1)(1-x)}{\alpha-\gamma}F'(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$
[9] $F'(\alpha,\beta-1,\gamma) = -\frac{(\beta-1)\alpha}{\beta-\gamma}F(\alpha,\beta,\gamma) + \frac{(\beta-1)(1-x)}{\beta-\gamma}F'(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$
Hieraus ist klar, dass man aus $F(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$ und $F'(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$ allgemein $F(\alpha+k,\beta+l,\gamma)$ und $F'(\alpha+k,\beta+l,\gamma)$ für jede ganze Werthe von k, und l, sie mögen positiv oder negativ seyn, rational ableiten kann.
Der Coëfficient von $x^r$ in $F(\alpha,\beta,\gamma-1)$ verhält sich, wie $\frac{\gamma-1+r}{\gamma-1}$, daher wird
[10] $F(\alpha,\beta,\gamma-1) = F(\alpha,\beta,\gamma) + \frac{x}{\gamma-1}F'(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$
Endlich sind die Coëfficienten in $xF'(\alpha,\beta,\gamma-1)$ und $F'(\alpha,\beta,\gamma-1)$ proportional den Zahlen $\frac{r(\gamma-1+r)}{\gamma-1}$ und $\frac{(\alpha+r)(\beta+r)}{\gamma-1}$, folglich der Coëfficient in $(1-x)F'(\alpha,\beta,\gamma-1)$ proportional $\frac{\alpha\beta+(\alpha+\beta+1-\gamma)r}{\gamma-1}$, also
[11] $F'(\alpha,\beta,\gamma-1) = \frac{\alpha\beta}{(\gamma-1)(1-x)}F(\alpha,\beta,\gamma) + \frac{(\alpha+\beta+1-\gamma)x}{(\gamma-1)(1-x)}F'(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$
Aus der Verbindung der Gleichungen 10 und 11 folgt endlich
[12] $F(\alpha,\beta,\gamma+1) = -\frac{(\alpha+\beta-\gamma)\gamma}{(\alpha-\gamma)(\beta-\gamma)}F(\alpha,\beta,\gamma) + \frac{\gamma(1-x)}{(\alpha-\gamma)(\beta-\gamma)}F'(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$
[13] $F'(\alpha,\beta,\gamma+1) = +\frac{\alpha\beta\gamma}{(\alpha-\gamma)(\beta-\gamma)x}F(\alpha,\beta,\gamma) - \frac{\gamma\gamma(1-x)}{(\alpha-\gamma)(\beta-\gamma)x}F'(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$

items.english: From this it is clear that from F(α,β,γ) and F′(α,β,γ) one can in general derive rationally F(α+k,β+l,γ) and F′(α+k,β+l,γ) for all integer values of k and l, whether positive or negative.
